title: SLO shadowing + sprint-bridge playbook (90d pilot)
content:
Purpose and elevator pitch:
This doc captures a 90-day pilot to operationalize SLOs through a lightweight cross-functional sprint bridge ("sprint-bridge") model. Goal: run 3 fast-fail experiments that validate observability, runbook automation, and stakeholder handoffs for model-serving SLOs so teams can move from ad-hoc incident response to repeatable SLO-driven operations.

Why this is different:
- Emphasis on "shadowing" product/feature teams for two-week windows to learn real fault modes rather than purely metric-driven hypotheses.
- Treat error-budget as an escrow that is visible to product owners and platform teams for tradeoff decisions.
- Combine runbook minimal automation with human-in-the-loop verification before full rollout.

High-level scope (90 days):
1) Week 0-2: Discovery + instrumentation gap sprint (prometheus metrics, trace spans, latency percentiles aligned across teams).
2) Week 3-6: SLO definition iterations + shadowing: 2 feature teams paired with SREs for live observations.
3) Week 7-10: Experiment 1 — Canary fallback automation for degraded models (automated fallback to quantized replica).
4) Week 11-14: Experiment 2 — Prefix/KV cache circuit and its effect on tail latency under burst traffic.
5) Week 15-18: Experiment 3 — Error-budget escrow dashboard + product signoff workflow.
6) Week 19-20: Retrospective, knowledge transfer, and rollout recommendations.

Key stakeholders and responsibilities:
- SRE Lead (Aisha Patel): overall pilot owner, facilitation, metrics signoff.
- Platform Eng (Marco Ruiz): canary automation, rollout tooling, CI integrations.
- Observability (Linnea Berg): metric definitions, trace instrumentation, dashboards.
- Product Owner (Omar Khan): feature team coordination, business impact assessment.
- Solutions Eng / CS (Priya Desai): customer-facing risk communications template.
- Oncall rotation reps (Evelyn Cho + two others TBD): validate runbook clarity during shadow windows.

Success criteria (measurable):
- SLOs are agreed and documented for 2 target services with clear SLI definitions and measurement windows (7d/30d).
- Runbook automation reduces manual step count by >=50% for the canary rollback play.
- Error budget dashboard displays live budget, burn rate, and a product signoff button; at least 1 product decision executed with the dashboard during pilot.
- Mean time to recovery (MTTR) for simulated latency incidents reduced by 30% in shadowed services.

Detailed play components (notes / run lists):
Discovery sprint (Week 0-2) checklist:
- Inventory of existing SLIs (p50/p95/p99 latency, qps, tail CPU/GPU queuing, model load time) for target services.
- Collect trace examples for 5 recent incidents (link to traces).
- Quick-gap telemetry fixes tracked as small PRs (label: slo-pilot-telemetry).

SLO definition workshop outputs:
- SLO template: "sli_name | query | window | target | measurement_source | owner" (e.g., generation-latency-p99 | histogram query | 30d | 99.5% | prometheus | feature-team-x).
- Default windows: 7d rolling for early detection, 30d for business SLA alignment.
- Error budget policy: burn < 2x baseline triggers low-touch comms; >2x triggers oncall pairing.

Shadowing protocol (two-week rhythm):
- Day 1: kickoff with product team, review runbook and SLO dashboard; confirm normal ops baseline.
- Day 2-9: SRE shadow participates in daily standups, monitors dashboards, annotates incidents and near-misses.
- Day 10: simulation day (synthetic latency spike or traffic surge under controlled canary).
- Day 11-14: post-sim analysis, update runbook, automation tickets.

Experiment 1: Canary fallback automation notes:
- Hypothesis: automated fallback to a compatible, quantized model variant will reduce tail latency spikes without impacting 95% of user queries.
- Success metric: tail latency (p99) reduction during spike >=25% and customer-facing error rate does not increase >0.1%.
- Steps: implement canary rule in platform router with health-check gating, include circuit-breaker thresholds, staged rollout to 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic.
- Safeties: manual abort button, immediate revert loop to previous model image, feature-team signoff for rollout beyond 25%.

Experiment 2: KV/prefix cache circuit:
- Hypothesis: enabling prefix caching with TTL heuristics reduces CPU/GPU occupancy during repetitive prompt patterns and improves latency for cache-hit cohort.
- Measurement plan: tag cached vs uncached request path; compare p95 and p99 latency and per-token cost across cohorts.
- Rollback plan: single feature flag with immediate disable and metrics pipeline to detect cache corruption.

Experiment 3: Error-budget escrow dashboard:
- Purpose: make burn-rate visible to product owners and enable explicit product tradeoffs (e.g., feature throttle, capacity purchase, or accept burn).
- UI/UX needs: live burn-rate sparkline, projected burn at current rate, product decision button with three choices and required justification text.
- Integration: Slack alerts to #product-slo-decisions when burn crosses thresholds.

Automation & infra tasks (owner tags):
- observability: add histogram buckets for model latency (Linnea).
- router: implement health-check gating for canary automation (Marco).
- dashboard: escrow view + decision action (Platform + Observability).
- runbooks: convert updated runbooks to runnable playbooks with small scripts for common steps (SRE).

Communications and gating:
- Weekly sync: 30m triage on Wednesdays with product and platform leads.
- Escalation path: if burn-rate > 3x projected and trending, immediate product pact meeting within 2 hours.
- Customer comms: Priya drafts a template for status updates and risk notices.

Risks and mitigations (quick list):
- Risk: inconsistent SLI definitions across teams -> Mitigation: one-hour SLI harmonization sync and Confluence canonical doc.
- Risk: dashboards undercount due to sampling -> Mitigation: increase scrape resolution for pilot services, validate with traces.
- Risk: automation flips too aggressively -> Mitigation: conservative thresholds, human approval step for >25% traffic changes.

Budget & staffing note:
- Expect ~0.2 FTE from observability team, ~0.3 FTE platform engineer during active experiment weeks, and 0.5 FTE SRE for shadow windows. Cost code: ENG-OPS-PILOT-26.

Open questions / decisions to make quickly:
- Which two feature teams are the pilot targets? (proposed: embeddings-service, chat-router)
- Do we use 7d or 14d windows as the default early-warning for product signoff?
- Minimum approval list for canary beyond 25% (product + SRE + platform required?)

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Lock pilot teams and calendar blocks: Aisha to send invites by Fri.
- Create telemetry PRs for required histograms and tracing tags (Linnea).
- Draft a short customer-facing risk notification template (Priya).
- Open canary automation spike ticket in GH and attach a minimal acceptance test (Marco).

Notes to self:
- Keep experiments small and observable; the goal is operational learning not perfect tooling.
- Document every manual decision during shadowing so we can automate the truly repetitive ones.
- Expect messy timelines; schedule two buffer weeks for instrumentation fixes.

Appendix: quick links and templates
- SLO template (to copy): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+Template
- Incident annotation template: /docs/incident-annotations.md (internal repo)
- Sample alert thresholds: see GH gist /sre/alert-thresholds/pilot.json

End of doc.
